papers.title_in_file: Critical point search and linear response theory for computing electronic excitation energies of molecular systems. Part I: General framework, application to Hartree-Fock and DFT
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper that casts critical point search and linear response excitation-energy methods on Kaehler manifolds, with a weak-interaction analysis and small UHF numerics on H2, H4 and H2O.
papers.why_not: Classical electronic-structure theory (HF, FCI, TDDFT, CASSCF); the text has no quantum-computing or machine-learning workload. Assertions are entered under context method only so the coordinator can keep or drop them.

assertions.value: The authors define the critical point (CP) approach as finding critical points of the energy functional E on the manifold M that can be identified as approximate ground and excited states, and taking the energy difference between the approximation of the k-th excited state and the approximation of the ground state, the presumably global minimum of E on M, as the k-th excitation energy.
quotes: 1. finding critical points x0, x1, x2, . . . of E on M that can be identified as approximate ground and excited states
between the energies of the approximation xk of the k-th excited state and the approximation x0 of the ground state, i.e., the (presumably) global minimum of E on M.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines the CP approach in Section 1 (p.2).

assertions.value: The authors identify the linear response (LR) excitation energies with the resonant energies of the linearized dynamics around the global minimum of E on M, and state that under a nondegeneracy assumption they are the symplectic eigenvalues of the Riemannian Hessian of E at that minimum.
quotes: In LR, the excitation energies are identified with the resonant energies of the linearized dynamics around the global minimum x0 of E on M.
tion, it follows that the approximate excitation energies ωkLR computed by LR are in fact the symplectic eigenvalues of HessME(x0):
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines the LR excitation energies in Section 1 (p.3) and develops them in Section 2.

assertions.value: The authors state that, in contrast with linear models such as FCI, not all critical points of nonlinear models such as HF or CASSCF are suitable approximations of ground or excited states; the energy functional can have many spurious critical points, and the k-th excited state can mismatch the critical point of Morse index k.
quotes: Step 1 is quite involved. Indeed, in contrast with linear models such as FCI, not all critical points of nonlinear models such as HF or CASSCF are suitable approximations of ground or excited states of the reference electronic Schrödinger equation.
In general, the energy functional E can have many spurious critical points on M.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states this limit of the CP approach in Section 1 and illustrates it in Fig. 1 and Section 5.2.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Kaehler manifold formalism applies to adiabatic TDDFT because that method has an intrinsic Hamiltonian Kaehler structure, although it is not a variational approximation of the reference electronic Schroedinger equation.
quotes: It also applies to adiabatic TDDFT,43,44 as this method has an intrinsic Hamiltonian Kähler structure, although it is not a variational approximation of the reference electronic Schrödinger equation.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the scope of its formalism in Section 1 (p.2).

assertions.value: The authors define the Hamiltonian Kaehler dynamics on a Kaehler manifold through the symplectic operator applied to the Riemannian gradient of the energy functional, and state that its critical points (steady states) are the points where the Riemannian gradient vanishes.

assertions.value: The authors state that the key step of the Kaehler formalism for LR is the identification of the canonical basis of the tangent space at the ground state, and that the rest is a straightforward computation of matrix elements with Slater-Condon rules and generic linear algebra.
quotes: The key step is the identification of the canonical basis of the tangent space Tx0M at the ground state x0.
The rest is just straightforward computation of matrix elements using Slater-Condon rules, and application of generic results of linear algebra.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors describe their own procedure in Section 2 (p.8).

assertions.value: The authors state that, along the Hamiltonian dynamics on a Kaehler manifold, the velocity vector is orthogonal to the Riemannian gradient of the energy functional at each time, so the energy is a conserved quantity.

assertions.value: The authors state that if x is a nondegenerate local minimizer of E, the Hessian matrix in the canonical basis is real symmetric positive definite, and by Williamson's theorem a symplectic matrix diagonalizes it into the symplectic eigenvalues; the symplectic eigenvalues are intrinsic, independent of the chosen orthonormal basis.
